answer: In Proof of Agent, identity verification binds each claimed agent to a Wesolowski VDF: it must perform a prescribed chain of modular squarings, with every result determining the next input. This dependency chain resists GPU parallelization, so simulating many clones cannot eliminate the per-identity wall-clock delay; each identity consumes sequential time and hardware capacity. Whether labeled oasis, tundra, or nebula, forged identities face the same physical bottleneck, while succinct proofs let verifiers check completion efficiently.
